tess: flagging a reproducible mismatch during node drain: prefill wrote resident metadata before lease was actually transferred, causing a stale tombstone to be served on a retry.
leo: can you paste the compact trace?
tess: yep. short trace: 
```
1) client read -> lease on nodeA
2) eviction triggers prefill on nodeB
3) nodeA locally DEMOTED prefix for reads but lease is still active
4) nodeB commits residency based on demote view
5) client retries and hits nodeA tombstone -> inconsistent state
```
anya: this is the demote vs lease visibility gap we've feared. the prefill commit must not assume demote == lease_release.
morgan: agreed. options we previously discussed: make demote+lease release atomic (requires big ownership refactor), epoch-guarded prefill commit, or a token/quiesce handshake.
leo: quick tradeoffs:
- atomic release: best for correctness, worst for drain latency and big change
- epoch-guard: small surface, aborts on mismatch, needs cleanup and backoff to avoid write storms
- token handshake: explicit contract, less aborts, more plumbing and token lifecycle mgmt
anya: for short-term, epoch-guard seems pragmatic. impl sketch: prefill reads lease_epoch E, prepares residency write but CASes on prefix.residency_epoch==E. if CAS fails abort and fallback to read-through. ensure partial writes are impossible via generation-tagged keys.
tess: couple of gotchas: (1) multi-writer races where two nodes both observed E and race to CAS; need deterministic winner semantics (first successful CAS wins). (2) aborted candidate entries must be cleaned or GCed.
morgan: for (1) first CAS wins is fine; losers fallback. for (2) we can write candidate with a short TTL and have a finalizer job to sweep stale candidates. also emit metric prefill_cas_failures.
leo: also instrument prefill_attempts_per_success and prefill_backoff_wait_seconds. we need SLO guardrails so prefill doesn't overload storage under heavy churn.
anya: test plan I'm proposing: unit tests for CAS success/fail, integration sim with node drain race, and an e2e canary that runs drain+prefill-heavy workload while collecting metrics. I'll own tests.
tess: I'll prototype the CAS patch: use existing generation-tag mechanism for prefix residency writes, add a candidate marker and finalizer that removes it on abort. small PR name: prefill/epoch-guard-cas.
morgan: if we see too many CAS aborts in canary, we'll consider adding a quiesce token layer as optimization. token design: request token from lease-holder, include token in prefill commit; commit only accepted if token still valid. cleaner but requires token routing.
leo: small operational note: add exponential backoff with jitter on prefill retry and a threshold where we stop retrying and let the client read-through. emit metric prefill_retries_before_giveup.
anya: one more corner: tombstone propagation timing. If lease-holder serves a tombstone after demote, we must ensure subsequent residency writes never reintroduce old tombstones. epoch-guard prevents overwriting with stale residency, but we should also ensure tombstone visibility rules consult lease epoch. will follow up in separate thread.
prefetch-bot: branch created: prefill/epoch-guard-cas -> https://git.internal/r/redwood/prefetch/epoch-guard-cas
tess: thanks. plan: merge small patch behind a feature flag, run canary with drain job, collect prefill_cas_failures and prefill_success_attempts, then decide on token if abort rate too high. leaving thread open for followups.
leo: :thumbsup:
